h1:
Koh Phangan Cafes & Brunch
11 Great Coffee Spots by the Sea
intro: Koh Phangan is about more than the Full Moon Party. The west coast around Srithanu and the port town of Thong Sala is the island's real cafe scene — specialty coffee roasted on-island, healthy brunch, fresh-baked pastries, and seaside spots where you can settle in for a long sunset. We've picked 11 places that are actually open, with a straight take on what each one does best and roughly what you'll pay.

blocks.html: Srithanu is the yoga-and-wellness hub of Koh Phangan, so cafes here lean toward vegan dishes, smoothie bowls, and a slow, chilled-out vibe. Thong Sala is the working port where the ferries come and go, with serious coffee shops you can sit and work in all day. The two areas are about 15–20 minutes apart by scooter, so cafe-hopping both in a single day is easy.

blocks.title: Before you head out to cafe-hop
blocks.html: Some roads on Koh Phangan are steep and very slippery, especially the hill climbs around Srithanu and Haad Yao. If you're not confident on a scooter, ride slowly, wear a helmet, and avoid riding in the rain. A lot of accidents on the island happen on these steep stretches.
Most places in Srithanu are either fully vegan or have plenty of vegetarian options. The mood is relaxed and you can linger, which makes it ideal for a late breakfast after a yoga class.

items.name: Karma Kafe
items.blurb: The most design-forward spot in Srithanu — it looks like it was lifted straight out of Canggu, Bali. Standouts are the avocado toast, smoothie bowls, sushi rolls, and a Thai tea latte you can order with coconut or almond milk. Every corner is photogenic, and they run community events now and then like film screenings and workshops.

items.name: Pure Vegan Heaven
items.blurb: A low-waste vegan cafe built almost entirely from bamboo. The menu runs from smoothie bowls and salads to vegan Thai food, tacos, quesadillas, sweet-potato pancakes, and breakfast burritos. It's become one of the defining cafes of Srithanu.

items.name: ETHOS Koh Phangan
items.blurb: A cafe with a small garden that also hosts yoga classes and events. The dish everyone talks about is the Purple Pancakes, colored naturally, paired with coffee that's done well. The leafy setting makes it a good spot to settle in for a slow morning.

items.name: Karma Kafe (coffee corner) / Seed to Feed
items.blurb: Seed to Feed is a garden cafe attached to a hydroponic farm, with greens picked from the beds right next door. Expect sandwiches, salads, organic Thai dishes, and specialty coffee and tea. It's relaxed and quiet — a good place to sit and work.

blocks.title: Want to taste deeper? Try a Koh Phangan food tour or cooking class
blocks.text: Half a day with a local who knows the lanes — or cooking a dish yourself — teaches you more than just eating. Book ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide.

blocks.html: Thong Sala is the most serious coffee district on the island, with on-island roasters and Australian-style cafes. It's a good fit for remote workers who want stable Wi-Fi and a big table.

items.name: Bubba's Coffee — Thong Sala
items.blurb: The most talked-about roaster on Koh Phangan, roasting its own beans on the island. The Thong Sala branch has an air-conditioned room inside and a terrace out back. Brunch standouts are eggs Benedict and house-made sourdough. Fast Wi-Fi, and free water brought to your table.

items.name: Indigo Specialty Coffee & Bakery — Thong Sala
items.blurb: A French-leaning cafe known for croissants and fresh-baked bread that many rate as the best on the island. The Thong Sala branch is comfortable for working — power outlets, big tables, and quiet. The menu also has chia pudding, shakshuka, and falafel.

items.name: Balance Specialty Coffee
items.blurb: A small spot tucked into the forest near Thong Sala that many call the best flat white on the island. It's seriously Australian-style — leafy, quiet, and built for people who love their coffee black or with just milk. No sea view here; it's all about the cup.

items.name: Dots Coffee
items.blurb: On the main road in Thong Sala, near Bangkok Bank and about 200 m from the Thong Sala pier. It does coffee, tea, and lemonade well and doubles as a co-working space, making it a handy stop before or after the ferry.

items.name: German Bakery by Achim
items.blurb: A roadside bakery in Thong Sala baking fresh sourdough and croissants daily — a good place to stock up on bread to take back to your room. The coffee is solid, and you can swap in alternative milks for a small extra charge.

blocks.html: For a cafe with a real sea view you'll need to head a little out of town. The west and northwest coast is the side for good sunsets, and several spots cling to clifftops or sit right on the beach.

items.name: What's Cup! (Haad Yao)
items.blurb: A clifftop cafe near Haad Yao with a full panoramic sea view. The brunch menu covers eggs Benedict, avocado toast, and pancakes, plus a full lineup of coffee and smoothies. It's a much-photographed sea-view corner, but the road up is fairly steep, so take the scooter slowly.

items.name: Footprint Cafe (Srithanu)
items.blurb: A lakeside cafe in the middle of Srithanu — calm and quiet, good for reading or working. The staff are friendly, vegan dishes start around THB 100, and there's free drinking water. The view is over the lake rather than open sea, but it's shaded and pleasantly cool.

blocks.text: Plan a one-day cafe hop: Srithanu to Thong Sala

items.activity: Start at Footprint Cafe on the Srithanu lake — first coffee plus a light brunch.
items.note: Quiet early on; good for reading before the crowd arrives.

items.activity: Move on to Karma Kafe or Pure Vegan Heaven, grab some photos and order a smoothie bowl.
items.note: Both are in the same area, an easy walk or short ride apart.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.title: Into Thong Sala for the coffee

items.activity: Ride into Thong Sala and stop at Bubba's Coffee for on-island roasted coffee and eggs Benedict.
items.note: About 15–20 minutes from Srithanu into town.

items.activity: Settle in to work or take a long break at Indigo or Balance — go to Balance if you like your coffee black.
items.note: Stable Wi-Fi and power outlets, ideal for remote work.

items.activity: Finish by riding up to Haad Yao for What's Cup! and the sea view in the soft late light.
items.note: The climb is steep — ride slowly and head back before it's fully dark to be safe.

blocks.title: Prices and seasons, straight up
blocks.html: Coffee and brunch on Koh Phangan run noticeably higher than on the mainland because everything has to come over by ferry. Most cappuccinos land at THB 70–100. Room rates on the island swing hard with the season too — nights near the Full Moon get pricier and fill up fast, so book ahead if you're coming then.

faq.q: Which Koh Phangan area has the best cafes?
faq.a: Srithanu is strong on vegan cafes and laid-back healthy brunch — think Karma Kafe and Pure Vegan Heaven. Thong Sala is the place for specialty coffee and work-friendly spots like Bubba's Coffee, Indigo, and Balance. The two areas are about 15–20 minutes apart by scooter, so you can do both in a day.

faq.q: Where are the sea-view cafes on Koh Phangan?
faq.a: What's Cup! on the Haad Yao clifftop has a panoramic sea view, great for photos and soft late-day light. Footprint Cafe in Srithanu has a calm, leafy lake view that's good for working. The climb up to Haad Yao is fairly steep, so ride your scooter carefully.

faq.q: How much does coffee cost on Koh Phangan?
faq.a: Most cappuccinos are THB 70–100, and brunch mains run THB 150–320. Prices are higher than on the mainland because ingredients have to come over by ferry. Some vegan spots in Srithanu start mains around THB 100.

faq.q: Which cafes are good for working with solid Wi-Fi?
faq.a: Thong Sala has the most options. Bubba's Coffee and Indigo have fast Wi-Fi, power outlets, and big tables. Dots Coffee doubles as a co-working space near the pier. Over in Srithanu, Footprint Cafe is quiet and good for settling in for a while.

faq.q: What are the opening hours, and when should I go?
faq.a: Most coffee shops open around 7:00–8:00 and run into the evening — Bubba's 7:00–17:00, Balance 7:00–16:30, Indigo until 22:30. Go in the morning or late morning to beat the crowds and catch the pastries while they're still fresh.
